newsitem.title: UK: Swissair /Cargolux link may boost Euro cargo.
newsitem.headline: Swissair /Cargolux link may boost Euro cargo.

text.p: A new European air cargo group could emerge from talks between Lufthansa Cargo AG and Swissair for the sale of the former's 24.5 percent stake in Cargolux Airlines International to Swissair, air cargo industry sources said.
Earlier today, Lufthansa confirmed newspaper reports that talks were underway, while a Swissair spokesman told Reuters Swiss Cargo and Cargolux, "were reviewing the possibilities for cooperation."
The two companies are looking at how they could cooperate optimally and it was still open whether this could lead to a takeover or a financial stake, he added.

Cargolux is Europe's largest scheduled all-cargo airline and it has three Boeing 747-400F long-range freighters with a further two for delivery in August and November this year. It also operates four Boeing 747-200s, including one on lease- back from the U.S.-based Atlas Air Inc.
The air cargo sources said closer cooperation, if finalised could help provide Swiss Cargo with extra capacity as part of a drive to strengthen its market position.

"Freighter capacity is one of a number of areas under consideration following our strategic decision to pursue cargo cooperation with Swissair," Pierre Wesner, Cargolux vice-president Europe, Africa and the Middle East told Reuters.
While no specific timetable had been fixed for finalising negotations, Cargolux hoped an agreement would be reached by the autumn, Wesner added.
The sources said they understood Swissair had approached Lufthansa over the sale of the latter's Cargolux's stake.

The move towards closer cooperation between the Swiss and Luxmebourg carriers also reflects that Swissair took over the global sales and marketing of the Belgian airline, Sabena SA 's freight on January 1 this year.
Sabena is now 49 percent owned by Swissair.

Luxembourg's geographical location and air cargo facilities close to the Benelux countries, France and Germany is suitable for trucking freight from those countries rather than to Zurich airport with its higher costs, the air cargo sources added.
Cargolux's Wesner added that continued cooperation between Cargolux and Lufthansa should not be ruled out in the event of Swissair acquiring the German carrier's stake.
"At present, Lufthansa has block bookings on our Boeing 747-400F services to the U.S. west coast -- Los Angeles," he said.
"There is no reason why this tried and tested agreement couldn't be maintained if there was a mind to do so...Certainly, we would be surprised if Swissair had reservations about it."

In other traffic sectors, Cargolux and Lufthansa were direct competitors in other regions of North America, the Far East and Africa, so the situation would not change with the arrival of Swissair as a shareholder, the official added.

Official data shows that Swissair carried 293,000 tonnes of scheduled freight in 1996, Cargolux 233,914 tonnes and Sabena 79,000 tonnes and the combined figure would have ranked them among the world's top 10 air cargo carriers.
